correctness.rationale: A shortest path cannot revisit the interior of a face: the chord in that face attains the ambient lower bound between the visits, with equality only for the straight segment. Positive-defect vertices cannot be interior points of a minimizing path, since one of the two angles at such a vertex must be less than π. An independent backward unfolding in target coordinates on a doubled integer lattice enumerated 28 opposite-face and 26 side-face paths, with the claimed candidates present and each unfolded source dominated at all four corners by one of the claimed candidates. The squared-distance difference is affine, so this is an exact whole-square bound; the candidate segments cross actual edges and realize the bound. Boundary targets follow by continuity. Integrating the disk on the source square, clipping the lateral strips at transverse half-width 1/2, and clipping each opposite-face sector at t=1/2−s gives exactly T,S,B. The latter edge bound switches when (3/2+s)^2+(1/2−s)^2=r^2; the extrema and branch endpoints have the stated values. In centered opposite-face coordinates 0≤n≤m≤1/2, the squared distance (2−m)^2+n^2 strictly decreases with m on every ray n=tm, giving the unique maximum 2 and the cutoff m=ε+t²ε²/4+O(ε³) uniformly in t. The tail area is eight sectors with Jacobian m, divided by six, giving both stated coefficients. Exact rational monomial integration using the m,n chart independently gave 1,23/18,451/180,331/56,389423/25200 at exponents 0,2,4,6,8, respectively.
residual_risks: The frozen random sample checks only corroborate the CDF; the continuous distribution and tail are established by integration and expansion, not by sampling.

evidence: At h=1, the average of (x²+y²)^k on S_1 is a polynomial integral over a rational polygon, with the same square, four rectangles and four triangles as in the frozen result.
The terminal density before normalization is 8r[π/4−arccos(√2/r)]. With r=2−t the angle is t/2+3t²/8+O(t³), so this density is 8t+2t²+O(t³). Integration and division by six give 2ε²/3+ε³/9+O(ε⁴).

value.rationale: The marked-center distribution is a natural object, but this record reevaluates a known specialization of the exact square-prism law. Its extra tabulated numbers and Taylor term are routine evaluations of the already explicit planar domain and density, and the record gives no distinct application requiring those particular values. The facewise organization adds subdivisions without a new geometric or probabilistic conclusion. No independently motivated surviving claim warrants repair.
residual_risks: The conclusion concerns the incremental contribution of this record, not the scientific interest of intrinsic distance laws generally.
